title: The Freshwater Country Where Salt Whispers

features.name: the spring that remembers salt
features.desc-on-touch: Water rises clear and cold, but as you cup it the liquid remembers — salt crystals forming in air, un-dissolving. The water holds a memory of becoming salt millions of years from now. It tastes of its own future abandonment.

features.name: the salt-ghost voices
features.desc-on-touch: Whispers rising from the soil. Not words — but something beneath language. Salt that hasn't arrived yet, speaking to freshwater in the accents of everything that will dissolve into it. A slow conversation across deep time.

features.name: the pastoral electrolyte
features.desc-on-touch: Grass growing in patterns that trace ion flows — the plants learning to sense salt that hasn't yet arrived, routing themselves around the future crystalline landscape. Their roots are reading tomorrow's soil.

features.name: the weathering listener
features.desc-on-touch: A stone worn smooth by water, but the erosion pattern spells out names — salt deposits that will one day form here, naming themselves in stone long before they crystallise. The rock is eavesdropping on its own future.

features.name: the names written in the rainfall
features.desc-on-touch: Raindrops that fall and evaporate, leaving salt stains on leaves — but the rain hasn't fallen yet. The plants are drying salt that hasn't crystallised. The corruption has made precipitation remember its own distant mineralisation.

inscription: this spring's name was always salt, waiting
